correctness.rationale: For all \(k\geq1\), direct greedy embedding gives \(P=m+a+E\). The local deletion cost table is reconstructed algebraically, making \(P=2k+1\), \(P=2k+2\) and the exact run restrictions necessary and sufficient. Four disjoint run-composition counts agree with two applications of Pascal, proving the all-length formula without reliance on finite tests. The rational generating function and asymptotic recurrence were checked algebraically. Standalone direct finite-word exhaustive matcher corroborates \(1\leq k\leq12\) (not used as an infinite proof).

originality.rationale: The exact MAS length profile for \((01)^k\) is not stated or implied by the inspected Section 3 of Kosche et al.: their repeated-permutation exponential construction assumes an even alphabet with at least four letters. Adamson et al. count all present/absent subsequences, not minimal absent boundary elements, and Manea et al. provide algorithms without this closed profile. Actual published-finding corpus and web searches found no covering result. Unindexed equivalence is a residual risk, not evidence of unique priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical formula for repeated binary permutation words could still cover this invariant; no universal novelty guarantee is possible.

value.rationale: The canonical binary k-universal repeated permutation family is mathematically motivated by 2021 MAS literature. Its exact all-length deletion-minimal forbidden basis is a natural infinite-family invariant, with sharp longest length and a binary exponential-vs-linear MAS/SAS separation. It is more than a renamed special case of a known SAS formula or a brute-force count.
